note: Flags do not block the merge (per owner instruction). Each flag lists its evidence source IDs (see sources.json) and the manual action needed. Flags FLG-015 to FLG-020 were added on 2026-11-13 by the integration with session 26634cd5 (see COORDINATION.md for the mapping of their F1 to F8).

flags.item: The three submitted identifiers are not 10-character ASINs
flags.detail: The identifiers in the submitted links are B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV. Each is 9 characters long. The official Creators API documentation shows ASIN examples of 10 characters (S06), and all three redirect targets use 10-character IDs (S14-S16). Typing amazon.com/dp/<each ID> returns 'Page Not Found' (S08-S10). No product name, brand, price, rating or commission can be tied to these identifiers. Confirmed by the GetItems reference (S06, chunk 1 of 3): an ASIN is a 10-character identifier.
flags.action: Provide the intended product page URL or 10-character ASIN for each product (the owner's input is needed; this session cannot infer it).

flags.item: Short links redirect to three different products, not confirmed as the submitted products
flags.detail: Each short link ended on a different amazon.com product page (S11-S13), and the mapping was the same on two fetches each. The final URLs carry the parameters lv=shuf and plpRedirect=mhFallback. The page titles identify two CHEFMAN air fryers and one Emeril Lagasse air fryer toaster oven (S14-S16). What these parameters mean is not documented in any official source reviewed, so they are recorded as observed only and never used as product data. The direct amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH request returns a 'Continue shopping' interstitial (S16), so product 3's title is only readable through the short link (S23).
flags.action: Open each submitted link in a normal browser and confirm where it lands. Confirm which product was intended.

flags.item: link.amazon links are not documented in the Associates policies reviewed and may be Redirecting Links
flags.detail: The Program Policies reviewed (S02) do not name link.amazon. The policies prohibit a link shortener that makes the Amazon destination unclear (PF-06, section 6(w)). They also disqualify purchases referred by a Redirecting Link, meaning a link that sends users through an intermediate site without a customer click (PF-07). The short links redirected automatically to amazon.com in the fetch tool (S11-S13). A third-party competitor claims link.amazon forwards to amzlinks.in (S17). That claim is not verified against any Amazon page.
flags.action: Test each link while logged in to an Associates account and record whether tracked clicks appear. Generate Special Links from Associates Central instead, if the owner wants to use them.

flags.item: Product name, brand, price, rating, review count, competitor count, best-seller rank and availability are unverified for all 3 products
flags.detail: The identifiers do not resolve (FLG-001), so no official product record exists to read these values from. The fetch tool returned only the page title and the URL for the redirect targets (S14-S16); prices and ratings were not in its text. These cells are left blank on purpose.
flags.action: After FLG-001 is fixed, read the values from the Creators API (see FLG-006) or the live product page, then add them to data/products.json with a source ID.

flags.item: Per-product commission rate cannot be assigned; the public Table 1 category rates can be stated
flags.detail: FLG-005 as originally written said 'the official rate schedule is not accessible' and implied commission rates are unavailable. That is only half true and is corrected here after re-verification on 2026-11-14: (1) affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/schedule DOES redirect to sign-in (re-confirmed 2026-11-14; S03) — but its return_to is /home/account/payment/customratecard, i.e. an account-specific custom rate card; (2) Amazon's Standard Commission Income Statement Table 1 IS public without a sign-in at S25 and was read in full on 2026-11-13 and again 2026-11-14 (Kitchen 4.50%, Home 3.00%, All Other Categories 4.00%, Luxury Beauty 10.00%, ... 11 rows). What remains unverified is the per-ASIN category assignment and any custom rate, so the per-product commission rate cells stay blank.
flags.action: Read the public Table 1 (S25) as a category reference — already done, see pricing and commission pages. Leave the per-product commission rate and commission-income estimate blank until the listing's category and a custom rate card (sign-in) are available.

flags.item: Automated product, price and review data needs Creators API access, which needs qualifying sales
flags.detail: The Creators API prerequisites require enrolment and 'at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days' (PF-16, S04). Price and availability may be shown only if the link serves them or they come from the API (PF-04). Reviews and star ratings may be shown only through the API (PF-05). Pulling this data from amazon.com pages instead would not meet these rules, so it was not done.
flags.action: Confirm Associates enrolment status. Once eligible, register for the Creators API (S04) and provide credentials through a secure secret store, never in the repo.

flags.detail: Branch arena/3c6cba43-zone3 (read-only, not edited) states that PA-API 5 is 'the only sanctioned data source'. The official PA-API 5 deprecation notice says it 'has been deprecated and is being replaced by the Creators API' (PF-17, S05). This site uses the Creators API as the data source.

flags.item: No Associates tag was supplied; no Special Links were created
flags.detail: Every Special Link must carry the Associates tag (PF-03, S02, section 2(b)). Without the owner's tag, no link on this site is a tracked Special Link. The submitted links carry only srctok and channelId parameters (S11-S13).
flags.action: Supply the Associates tag (not a password or token) so Special Links can be built and tested.

flags.item: No click or conversion data exists; the campaigns ledger is empty on purpose
flags.detail: Click and conversion figures come only from the owner's Associates reports, which need a logged-in account. Tracking rules are recorded (PF-12, PF-13). No click or conversion value has been invented.
flags.action: Export the Associates reports for the tag once Special Links are live, then add them with source references.

flags.item: No SEO articles, comparisons or buying guides were written
flags.detail: Content would need verified product facts (PF-10 forbids inaccurate or misleading product claims) and first-hand experience that has not happened (PF-21). Writing copy from the redirect titles would present unconfirmed products as the submitted ones. The content section records what is blocked and why.
flags.action: After FLG-001 and FLG-004 are resolved, the content pipeline can generate drafts from verified data for owner review.

flags.item: Disclosure is in the footer; placement needs owner review
flags.detail: The required statement (PF-01) is on every page. The FTC asks that a disclosure be hard to miss and placed with the endorsement (PF-20). The footer may not meet that standard for a product recommendation. Account enrolment could not be checked from this session. Re-verified 2026-11-14: the FTC Endorsement Guides were revised in 2023 (S24) and the FTC's current plain-language brochure is 'Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers' (S07). FTC guidance is that a disclosure must be hard to miss and placed near the endorsement (PF-19, PF-20); a footer-only statement is the weakest compliant position.
flags.action: Owner: review the placement and confirm the Associates account is active.

flags.item: Source pages show different copyright years
flags.detail: The Associates Operating Agreement and Program Policies show a footer of '© 1996-2025'. The Amazon product pages show '© 1996-2026'. Both were read on 2026-11-13. The header dates (S01: October 15, 2025; S02: April 14, 2026) were used as the versions read.
flags.action: None required. Re-check the policy version before each content update.

flags.item: Associates site eligibility for an Oslo-based site is not stated; Schedule 1 lists only the United States
flags.detail: Operating Agreement Schedule 1 lists one location, United States, with amazon.com. The text read does not say whether an Associate in Norway may use amazon.com links, and the Norwegian Amazon site is not listed. All three resolved links are amazon.com (US). This was raised by session 26634cd5 as F3.
flags.action: Owner: confirm in Associates Central which Amazon sites the account may link to, before publishing any link.

flags.item: The AI analysis layer cannot use Creators API data without written approval
flags.detail: Creators API terms bar aggregating, analysing or repurposing Product Advertising Content without express prior written approval, and bar using Program Content to develop or train machine learning or language models (PF-23, PF-24, PF-25). The brief asks for an AI-powered platform. Any AI analysis of Amazon data is therefore blocked until approval is obtained. No AI analysis of Amazon data has been built.
flags.action: Owner: request written approval from Amazon for the planned analysis before building it, or limit the analysis to data the site already displays.

flags.item: The FTC guidance used is from 2019; the Endorsement Guides were revised in 2023
flags.detail: The FTC brochure in S07 is dated November 2019. The FTC topic page (S24) states that the Endorsement Guides were 'revised in 2023'. The current guides were not read. The disclosure text used on the site is the Associates wording (PF-01), which is verified; the FTC points are not used as a finding.
flags.action: Read the 2023 Endorsement Guides on ftc.gov before publishing marketing copy.

flags.item: Claim on reviews created in exchange for compensation withdrawn
flags.detail: The earlier fact PF-14 quoted text attributed to the Operating Agreement that was not found in any section read on 2026-11-13. It has been removed from policy_facts.json and is not stated anywhere on the site.
flags.action: None. Re-add only with a verbatim quote from the official page.

flags.item: Automation needs rules that have not been built: caching, price date stamps, disclaimers, agent identification, no scraping
flags.detail: The Creators API terms limit caching (PF-26), require a date and time stamp next to price or availability (PF-27), require a disclaimer (PF-28), cap call rates and file sizes (PF-29), require agents to identify themselves (PF-31), and forbid data mining and robots (PF-22). Program Content may be used only for Amazon products (PF-32), and click generation and price tracking are prohibited (PF-33, PF-34). None of this automation has been built.
flags.action: Design the data layer around these rules before any automation is built.

flags.item: Product 3 direct URL returns a 'Continue shopping' page
flags.detail: amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH returns a 'Continue shopping' interstitial rather than a product page (S16). The title of product 3 is only readable through the short link (S23). This matches session 26634cd5's F6.
flags.action: Open the listing in a browser and confirm the title.

flags.item: Kitchen reference rate 4.50% is verified, but the listings' category is not
flags.detail: Amazon's Standard Commission Table 1 lists 'Kitchen' at 4.50% (S25; PF-38). The Onsite Table A lists 'Kitchen' at 1.25% for Onsite Content only (S26; PF-39). Neither is a product rate. To know which row applies, the category of each listing is needed. The product category is not stated in the text of the listings read (they show 'Home & Kitchen' as the department). The rate is therefore shown as a reference only and not on any product row. Raised by session 66a80e53 (PR #3).
flags.action: Owner: confirm each listing's category in Associates Central (or via the Creators API, once approved) before using any rate.

flags.item: Board statements that the commission rate card is unavailable are superseded by the public Table 1 (S25)
flags.detail: FLG-005 and FLG-013 in data/flags.json, and the earlier note 'Rates are not stated anywhere on the site' in COORDINATION.md, treat the rate card as sign-in-only. Re-verified 2026-11-14: only the /help/operating/schedule route is gated (and it returns an account customratecard); the Standard and Onsite Income Statement help node pages (S25, S26) render the full tables to anonymous users. Both were read again in this session. The published tables match what two other sessions recorded. No per-product rate is claimed from them.
flags.action: No action required on the tables themselves. Read FLG-005 (rewritten) and FLG-013 (scope narrowed) for what is still unverified.

flags.item: FLG-003's wording overstates what the policies say about link.amazon
flags.detail: FLG-003 says the links 'may not be trackable'. What the documents actually support, re-read verbatim on 2026-11-14, is narrower: Participation Requirements 6(w) prohibits a link shortener used in a way that makes it unclear you are linking to an Amazon Site (S02); Commission Income Statement 2(e) disqualifies purchases made through a 'Redirecting Link' (S30); 6(v) prohibits cloaking or obscuring the URL (S02). Whether link.amazon is itself such a link is a judgement on its behaviour, which was observed but is not addressed by name in any document read.
flags.action: Read as: do not publish link.amazon short links; publish canonical /dp/<ASIN> URLs with the Associates tag once a tag exists. Confirm with Amazon before using link.amazon at all.
